lines.t: Why does gas cost three ninety-nine and nine tenths? Who pays nine tenths of a cent?
lines.title: $3.99 *⁹⁄₁₀*

lines.t: It started in the Great Depression. Gas was so cheap, some places charged under ten cents a gallon.
lines.title: THE *1930s*

lines.t: At ten cents, raising the price by one full penny was a ten percent jump. So stations used fractions.
lines.title: ONE PENNY = *10%*
lines.label: of a 10¢ gallon

lines.t: Gas got expensive. The fraction never left. Because your brain reads three ninety-nine, not four dollars. It's called left-digit bias.
lines.title: LEFT-DIGIT *BIAS*

lines.t: And those tiny fractions add up. One estimate says around half a billion dollars a year in the U.S.
lines.title: TINY FRACTIONS, *BIG MONEY*
lines.label: Estimate · Marketplace

lines.t: Iowa actually banned it in nineteen eighty-five… and brought it back four years later.
lines.title: IOWA *TRIED*

lines.t: Did you ever notice the nine tenths? Follow for more price tricks.
lines.title: NOW YOU'LL *SEE IT*
